findings.title: Core model class MYNET (models/mel/Network.py) is absent; repo cannot run
findings.claim: fscil_trainer.py imports `MYNET` from `models/mel/Network.py` and instantiates it at line 30 (`self.model = MYNET(self.args)`), but no file `Network.py` exists under models/mel/ (only fscil_trainer.py and helper.py are present) and no `class MYNET` is defined anywhere in the repo (verified by grep over all .py files).
findings.concern: The proposed method itself is missing: MYNET is the whole contribution — the meta-category vector and attention masks (Eqs 4-6), feature-space transformation (Eq 10), the L_high/L_low/L_mutual heads (Eqs 11-14), the fc/part_fc classifiers, and encode1/update_fc — so `python train.py` fails at import (ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'models.mel.Network') and not a single value in Tables 1-6 or Figures 3-9 can be reproduced from this code.
findings.resolution: Authors: please add the missing models/mel/Network.py defining MYNET (with forward returning logits1, logits2, x1, part; plus encode1, update_fc, attention, fc, part_fc, mode), so the released code matches the trainer that imports it.

findings.title: Dataloaders for 3 of 4 evaluated datasets (CUB200, Stanford Cars, FGVCAircraft) absent
findings.quote:
if args.dataset == 'cub200':
    import dataloader.cub200.cub200 as Dataset
findings.claim: set_up_datasets imports `dataloader.cub200.cub200` (line 7), `dataloader.StanfordCar.StanfordCar` (line 24), and `dataloader.Aircraft.Aircraft` (line 32), but the only dataloader package present is `dataloader/StanfordDog/`; the cub200, StanfordCar, and Aircraft packages do not exist.
findings.concern: Running the code on any dataset other than StanfordDog raises ModuleNotFoundError, so the CUB200, Stanford Cars, and FGVCAircraft results (Table 1; Tables 3, 5, 6; Figure 3 a,c,d) have no runnable data-loading code even if the model file existed.
findings.resolution: Authors: please add the cub200 / StanfordCar / Aircraft dataloader modules matching the four `set_up_datasets` configs.

findings.title: No code for Fig 8/9 benchmarks & backbones, Fig 4 strategy variants, or Table 1 baselines
findings.quote:
def ResNet12():
    r"""ResNet-18 model from
    `"Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition" <https://arxiv.org/pdf/1512.03385.pdf>`_
    Args:
        pretrained (bool): If True, returns a model pre-trained on ImageNet
        progress (bool): If True, displays a progress bar of the download to stderr
    """
    return resnet12(ResNet12Block, [1, 1, 1, 1], drop_rate=0, max_pool=True)
findings.claim: ResNet-12 is the only backbone factory in the repo, and set_up_datasets (data_utils.py) defines only the four fine-grained datasets; there is no code/config for the conventional-benchmark experiments (Figure 8: miniImageNet, CIFAR100), the alternate backbones (Figure 9: ResNet-18/50, ViT-B/16, ViT+adaptor), the meta-category strategy variants (Figure 4: Avg, Avg+Sim, Avg+Weight, BP), or the Table 1 baseline methods.
findings.concern: Several reported experiments (Figs 4, 8, 9 and all Table-1 baseline columns) cannot be reproduced or checked because no corresponding backbone, dataloader, or driver code is present in the repository.
findings.resolution: Authors: please add (or point to) the code/configs for the conventional-benchmark and alternate-backbone experiments and the meta-category optimization-strategy ablations.

findings.title: No dependency specification; unusual unlisted dependency torch_dct
findings.claim: helper.py requires the third-party package `torch_dct` (imported here, though never used — a dead import), yet the repo contains no requirements.txt, environment.yml, setup.py, or pyproject.toml anywhere (verified by find over the tree); torch, numpy, tqdm, torchvision, and PIL are likewise unlisted/unpinned.
findings.concern: The runtime environment cannot be rebuilt deterministically, and importing models.mel.helper fails unless the undeclared torch_dct is installed.
findings.resolution: Authors: add a pinned requirements.txt / environment.yml, and remove the unused torch_dct import if it is not needed.

findings.title: Incremental few-shot support is drawn from the test split and overlaps the eval test set
findings.quote:
def SelectfromTxt(self, data2label, index_path):
    index = [x.strip().split('/')[2] for x in open(index_path, 'r').readlines()]
    target_by_class = {}
    for name in index:
        img_path = os.path.join(self.IMAGE_PATH, name)
        target_by_class[name.split('_')[0]] = data2label[img_path]

    csv_path = osp.join(self.SPLIT_PATH, 'test.csv')
    lines = [x.strip() for x in open(csv_path, 'r').readlines()][1:]
    data_tmp = []
    targets_tmp = []
    for class_name, target in target_by_class.items():
        names = [line.split(';')[0] for line in lines
                 if line.split(';')[0].split('_')[0] == class_name][:5]
        for name in names:
            data_tmp.append(os.path.join(self.IMAGE_PATH, name))
            targets_tmp.append(target)

    return data_tmp, targets_tmp
findings.claim: For incremental sessions (train=True, base_sess falsy), the few-shot support set is built by reading the session index file only to recover the novel class names, then selecting the FIRST 5 images per novel class from `test.csv` (line 105). The actual few-shot image list in data/index_list/StanfordDog/session_*.txt (which contains train-split images) is ignored. My check reproduces this: for session 1, all 25 selected support images come from test.csv, all 25 are also members of the incremental test set (which is likewise built from test.csv for all seen classes), and 0/25 match the real session_2.txt few-shot list.
findings.concern: The novel-class few-shot samples used to build the prototypes and to update the meta-category vector are a subset of the images they are then evaluated on, i.e. train/test leakage that inflates novel-class accuracy across the incremental sessions (Table 1 Stanford Dogs, Table 2 ablation, Table 4).
findings.resolution: Authors: confirm whether the released loader is what produced the reported numbers; the support should be read from the train split (the session_*.txt images), disjoint from the evaluation set — change `test.csv` at line 105 to the train split (or load the session_*.txt images directly).

findings.title: Optimizer excludes module.encoder.* from all param groups — backbone may never train
findings.claim: get_optimizer builds a param list that excludes every parameter whose name starts with `module.encoder.`, and the SGD optimizer is given only that list plus `model.module.attention`; so any submodule named `encoder` receives no gradient step during base training.
findings.concern: If MYNET's ResNet-12 backbone is registered as `self.encoder`, the feature extractor would never be updated in the base session, contradicting the paper's central claim of training/evolving fine-grained feature extraction (Insight 0, Section 3.3.1) — but this cannot be confirmed because the MYNET definition is missing.
findings.resolution: Authors: confirm the attribute name of the backbone inside MYNET and whether excluding `module.encoder.*` from the optimizer is intentional; if the backbone is `encoder`, clarify how it is trained in the base session.
